Study method details: 21 patient samples with triglycerides > 15 mmol/L, total lipids (cholesterol plus triglycerides) > 20 mmol/L, a lipaemic index > 3 and total protein within the reference interval (62-83 g/L); analysed before and after ultracentrifugation (Airfuge, 15 min at 107 000g) by indirect ISE potentiometry and by direct ISE; the ultracentrifuged indirect ISE result and the non-ultracentrifuged direct ISE result were each subtracted from the non-ultracentrifuged indirect ISE result; a second, prospective subset of 24 hyperlipidaemic samples was used to validate the correction formulas
Additional sources of bias: Small samples (n = 21 first subset, n = 24 second subset); the K effect is described as being to a lesser degree than for Na and Cl; no baseline or final K concentrations are printed anywhere in the letter; the supporting data are in an online Data Supplement (Fig. 1) that is not part of this PDF; total protein was constrained to the reference interval, so the lipid effect is isolated but the combined lipid-plus-protein case is not characterised (the authors explicitly caution about hyperlipidaemia complicated by hypo- or hyperproteinaemia)
